Run it against the CURRENT (unfixed) legend text and observe RED (the legend today does say 'a top-level tests package'); capture the real output; attest c1. Then reword SPLIT_LEGEND in BOTH scripts/code_map/render.py and scripts/code_map/checks.py by hand (mirror the edit in each file separately -- do NOT collapse them into an import; that independence is load-bearing per the reviewer's proof) so the sentence states 'a tests package anywhere on the module path' instead of 'a top-level tests package'. Do NOT touch is_test_module's predicate body in either file. Run the tc38 gate selector and observe GREEN; check c2.

why_trail.why: Baseline understood: is_test_module ends 'return "tests" in parts' -- a tests segment ANYWHERE on the dotted path -- but SPLIT_LEGEND in both render.py:361 and checks.py:301 says 'a top-level tests package'. Commander ruling is to fix the legend, keep the predicate, add a pinning check. Plan is 3 vertical slices matching the handoff's 3 pieces.

Reworded SPLIT_LEGEND in both render.py:361 and checks.py:301 by hand (no import): 'a top-level tests package' -> 'a tests package anywhere on the module path'. is_test_module's body untouched in both files (grepped -- zero diff there). tc38 selector -k 'refs or caller or legend' now collects 20 (up from 19 baseline), all green.

measure_split.py now cross-tabulates bucket x definer via checks.is_test_module on each page's own title module, reusing the reviewer's g5_reviewer_split_by_definer.py logic as the canonical script. Output matches the handoff table exactly: unused 88 prod / 2340 test, test-only 2 prod / 449 test, production 873 prod / 0 test. Corrected headline: genuinely unused production code is 88, not the naive 2428 (2340/2428 = 96.4% of that bucket is test-defined). Evidence written to .agent-work/issue-456/evidence/g5_remediate_split_by_definer.json.

Full suite green: 1781 passed, 2 skipped, 672 subtests, 0 failed in 356.75s (baseline+1, the new pinning test) -- confirmed independently by Commander too. Fresh build+check: modules 111, entities 3753, pages 3865 (baseline 3752/3864 +1 -- the new pinning test I wrote in m1 is itself a new mapped entity, since this repo's code_map indexes its own tests/ tree). check -> 7/7 exit 0. checks.py still imports nothing from render.py (independence intact, confirmed by grep). Re-ran measure_split.py against the fresh tree: exactly one cell moved by +1 (unused_test_defined 2340->2341, the new test itself, correctly bucketed as unused+test-defined since nothing calls it) -- the other five cells (88/2/449/873/0) are byte-identical to the handoff table, proving zero EXISTING entities were reclassified. Corrected m3's c2 hardcoded counts via amend (retext-check) since my own plan hadn't anticipated the self-indexing +1.

amendments.reason: My own plan hardcoded the pre-remediation baseline counts (111/3752/3864) into m3's c2 check. That baseline did not account for the fact that this repo's code_map indexes its own tests/ tree, so the new pinning test I added in m1 (test_the_legend_states_the_rule_the_predicate_actually_applies) is itself a new mapped entity. Verified independently: fresh build now reports (111,3753,3865), check is 7/7 exit 0, and re-running measure_split.py shows exactly one bucket moved by exactly +1 (unused_test_defined 2340->2341) with all five other cells unchanged (88/2/449/873/0) -- the new entity landed in the correct bucket (unused, test-defined, zero callers is its normal expected state) and zero EXISTING entities were reclassified. Correcting the hardcoded numbers to match, per Commander's own confirmation that the suite is green and split numbers match.
